definition: The houses the composer proposes for a brief: several contrasting plans, each seeded from a canonical plan diagram, ranked and never called good. Each says what it trades away and what it assumed where the brief was silent.
basis: Editorial. docs/compose.md: "Seed from the canonical partis." and "Rank fatal-free first, then by score." README.md: the composer returns candidates "each with what it trades away and a log of every assumption it made." VISION.md: "Several candidates, never one — and never call a plan good." "The generator returns contrasting options, ranked, each stating" what it trades away, "and it declines to endorse any of them."

surface.what: The houses composed from your brief, ranked and never called good.
read: Each candidate starts from a canonical plan diagram, native to the style where one exists.
A candidate with no fatal error ranks above any that has one; after that, they are ranked by score.
Each says what it trades away and lists what it assumed where the brief was silent.
Open one on the bench to work on it.
